item.title: Why does Elon Musk want to put a million satellite data centres in space?
item.description:
The Trump administration has approved Elon Musk’s plan to create datacentres in space. US federal regulators have authorised the launch of one million Starmind orbital satellites, which are built by Musk’s SpaceX, to process data in space. Supporters argue the project will be more energy-efficient and reduce the environmental impact of datacentres on Earth as the AI industry grows. But how realistic is the plan and what could the consequences be? Michael Safi speaks to Guardian global technology editor Dan Milmo Continue reading...

item.title: Open Thread
item.description:
People share food at the dinner table during Thanksgiving. —Stock photo—Getty Images As households across America prepare to gather for their Thanksgiving celebrations , there’s one question at the forefront of hosts’ minds: what time should dinner be served? A quick glance on social media will tell you that it’s a hotly-debated topic, and one that people have firm opinions on. Lifestyle expert Martha Stewart’s online publication conducted a poll in 2024, asking readers what time Thanksgiving dinner should start. More than 34,000 people joined the conversation, with the majority of respondents (13,586) saying the meal should begin between 2 to 3 p.m., local time. Stewart is also a proponent of these timings, telling the Today show last year that she believes dinner should be served at 2 p.m., as “people are hungry” and are likely already starting to “circle the kitchen.” But preferences…

item.title: New Zealand election results set up tricky talks for conservative incumbent
item.description:
Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls. Preliminary results on 7 November handed the National party and its two coalition partners, the populist New Zealand First and libertarian Act parties, a slim two-seat majority, making the election too close to call until final votes were tallied. item.title: Hakeem Jeffries has disarmed a progressive revolt, but can he deliver?
item.description:
After years of being able to hide behind Republicans’ blatant mismanagement and intentional sabotage of the healthcare system, Democrats will now have to put forth their own plan to save our crumbling healthcare infrastructure. Whether the party can agree on what that plan is remains to be seen. The middle path has been dubbed “Medicare for More.” It’s been framed variously as a first step toward Medicare for All and as a half-measure to relieve the pressure to pass the more expansive healthcare agenda. Now backed by Rep.
